stem: Which statement best describes a narrow therapeutic index drug?

options.A: Small changes in dose or blood concentration can produce important loss of efficacy or serious toxicity, so dosing and monitoring require particular care.
options.B: The drug has a wide separation between effective and toxic exposure, so modest concentration changes rarely affect therapeutic safety or efficacy.
options.C: Blood concentration and clinical response have little relationship to safety, making therapeutic monitoring generally unhelpful for this type of drug.
options.D: Dose changes can be made in large increments because the therapeutic window is broad and toxicity usually occurs far above effective concentrations.

rationale: FDA describes narrow therapeutic index drugs as having a tight therapeutic window in which small differences in dose or blood concentration may lead to therapeutic failure or serious adverse effects, including life-threatening toxicity or significant disability. FDA also notes that these drugs require careful dosing and patient monitoring, with therapeutic drug monitoring used for many NTI drugs. Therefore A is correct. B and D describe a wide therapeutic index, while C contradicts the recognized importance of concentration-response relationships and monitoring in NTI therapy.
educational_objective: Explain why narrow therapeutic index drugs require precise dosing and, when indicated, close clinical or laboratory monitoring.
source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
source_document_title: Setting and Implementing Standards for Narrow Therapeutic Index Drugs
source_locator: What are narrow therapeutic index drugs?: small differences in dose or blood concentration may lead to therapeutic failures or life-threatening/significantly disabling adverse effects; NTI drugs have little separation between therapeutic and toxic doses and require careful dosing and patient monitoring.
source_claim_supported: NTI drugs have a narrow margin between effective and harmful exposure, so small dose/concentration changes can have major consequences and careful dosing/monitoring is required.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — therapeutic drug safety and monitoring.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only absolute wording and balanced option lengths while preserving FDA's NTI definition and monitoring implications.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — FDA directly defines NTI drugs by clinically consequential small dose/concentration differences and careful monitoring; A uniquely matches.
